_readme: Studio facts used across the site: the footer, the press fact sheet, structured data and llms.txt. Change a fact here and every page that states it follows on the next build. log is the dated history on the home page, newest last; photo is a name from data/images.json.
name: Shiverbug Studios
registeredOffice: Victoria Building, Victoria Road, Middlesbrough, TS1 3AP, United Kingdom

log.label: May 2025
log.text: Three Teesside University graduates, Lewis Mennim, Ryan Hughes and Garrett Windus, set up Shiverbug Studios Ltd in Middlesbrough.

log.label: June 2025
log.text: Picked as one of 21 teams for Tranzfuser 2025, the government-funded programme for new graduate studios, with Teesside Launchpad as our local hub.

log.label: September 2025
log.text: Took our prototype, then called Koopa and Kiko, to ProtoPlay in Dundee, and came home as the Tranzfuser 2025 Public Vote Winner.
log.alt: Lewis, Ryan and Garrett on stage at ProtoPlay 2025 holding the Tranzfuser Public Vote Winner certificate, beside a ProtoPlay organiser.
log.caption: ProtoPlay, Dundee. The certificate says the most votes of any Tranzfuser team.

log.label: November 2025
log.text: Joined Game Republic, the games industry network for the North of England.

log.label: January 2026
log.text: Started the game again in a fresh Unity 6 project, the one that became Out of Water, and gave the studio a new logo and a mascot: Shana the Shiverbug, the moth on every page of this site.

log.label: February 2026
log.text: Told the world what the game is about. A turtle, a seagull and five stolen gems.

log.label: April 2026
log.text: Put Out of Water in front of players at the Odyssey video games and toy festival in Harrogate.

log.label: May 2026
log.text: The first of our Teesside interns joined the team.

log.label: July 2026
log.text: Seven of us went down to Develop:Brighton.
log.alt: Seven of the Shiverbug team on Brighton seafront in the sun, wearing Develop:Brighton lanyards, some in studio t-shirts.
log.caption: Brighton seafront, between talks.
